He is saying that video compression is basically ignoring small fast moving objects. I do not believe this to be the case. You would expect any effects from too low a accuracy settings and motion to cause them to pixelate, not disappear. Also every 16 frames or so, a complete image is rendered that does not depend on previous frames, so it should blink into view occasionally if it were related to the motion. It also cannot be too small to resolve because other things in the picture that are much smaller are resolving fine.

In order to use less data, video compression applies of a model of what regular people watching regular videos are most likely to notice or not. Whatever information it thinks you're the least likely to notice, it leaves out. The simpler it can make the video, the less information has to be transmitted.

When the casings are ejected we see them briefly while they are close to the camera, but as they fall away they become relatively small details in the background. The compression algorithm figures that these small details in the background are not that important so it does not update the background image.

Moreover, in order to show the casing up close, a significant burst of data was used, so now the algorithm needs to conserve data elsewhere in order to maintain whatever average data rate it is targeting. This takes away from the budget that can be used to update the background.

Similarly, a magician using slight of hand relies on you paying attention to the "big" thing an not the little details happening elsewhere.

Next time you are watching an action movie, notice that when large explosions are taking place you will see less details elsewhere in the scene.

It should be noted that designers of products like IP Security cameras are well aware of the limitations of video compression for forensic purposes. And for this reason they design their products with different compression algorithms and sometimes many tunable parameters, for example to help you designate which parts of the image you really care about (like where a license plate might appear).
